reply:
Still no. The Fetch API spec forbids GET bodies and throws on construction—that's what you're hitting. You're right that HTTP allows GET bodies with undefined semantics, but Fetch (the browser implementation) rejects them per [the spec](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-http-request):

> If the method is GET or HEAD, set body to null and unset body.

If you try to set a body anyway, the constructor throws `TypeError: Request with GET/HEAD method cannot have body`.

What would change my mind: evidence this works in a modern browser (run it and paste the result).

The fix: use POST, or move the query to the URL as a query string.
